title: Lift finite-level presentation kernels to completed free kernel vectors
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal, B its I-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and T an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system] annihilated at level n by I^(n+1), with surjective successor maps whose kernels are I^(n+1)T_(n+1). Let N be a B-module and e an A-linear isomorphism Res_A N to lim T satisfying the completed scalar residue equation [lem-weil-pbc-adic-tower-completed-scalar-limit]. Let d be a natural number and q a surjective B-linear map from the I-adic completion of A^d to N. If y maps to zero under q followed by the nth projection of e, there exists z with q(z)=0 and with the same evaluation in A^d/I^(n+1)A^d as y. No finiteness or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 087W, proof: Lift finite-level presentation kernels to completed free kernel vectors

proof.text: Identify the completed finite free module with a finite product of B. The scalar residue equation on its basis vectors shows that each composite p_n q depends only on the nth free residue. Thus it induces compatible A-linear presentations P_n -> T_n. The tower projections are surjective by recursive lifting along the surjective successors. Thus each composite p_n q is surjective because q is; its factor P_n → T_n is surjective.

Define K_n as the presentation kernel. Lift a K_n vector to P_(n+1); its image is in the transition kernel I^(n+1)T_(n+1). Lift an I^(n+1) correction through the surjective presentation and subtract it, proving surjectivity of K_(n+1) -> K_n.

The nth residue of y lies in K_n. Surjective kernel tower projections lift it to a compatible kernel sequence. Interpret this sequence as z in the free completion; all projections of e(q(z)) vanish, so q(z)=0 by limit extensionality and injectivity of e. Its nth residue is the residue of y.

theorem adicTower_freeKernelCorrection (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (T : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (hzero : ∀ n : ℕ, I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A (T.obj (op n))) = ⊥)
    (htrans : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Function.Surjective (T.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ∧
      LinearMap.ker (T.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom =
        I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A (T.obj (op (n + 1)))))
    (N : ModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I A))
    (e : (restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).obj N ≅ limit T)
    (hscalar : ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : AdicCompletion I A) (a : A) (x : N),
      AdicCompletion.evalₐ I (n + 1) r = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)) a →
      (e.hom ≫ limit.π T (op n)) (r • x) =
        a • (e.hom ≫ limit.π T (op n)) x)
    (d : ℕ) (q : AdicCompletion I (Fin d → A) →ₗ[AdicCompletion I A] N)
    (hq : Function.Surjective q) (n : ℕ) (y : AdicCompletion I (Fin d → A))
    (hy : (e.hom ≫ limit.π T (op n)) (q y) = 0) :
    ∃ z : AdicCompletion I (Fin d → A), q z = 0 ∧
      AdicCompletion.eval I (Fin d → A) (n + 1) z =
        AdicCompletion.eval I (Fin d → A) (n + 1) y
